transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Um, yeah… thanks. I guess I’m here because I’ve been having a really hard time sitting still. Like, in the radiology suite or in class, when I’m supposed to just stay put and focus, I start feeling like I’m crawling out of my skin.

I’ve tried to just push through it for months and not make a big deal out of it, but I still end up pacing, shifting around a lot, or finding some excuse to get up and move. I don’t know if that makes sense, but it’s been getting hard to manage.
Have you started or changed the dose of any medications, especially any antipsychotic or anti-nausea drugs, around the time this restlessness began?

Um… I don’t think so. I mean, I’m not on anything like that that I know of, and I haven’t changed doses of anything around when this started. At least… not that I can think of. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

When you feel this need to move, is it mainly an uncomfortable sensation in your legs that gets better when you move them, and does it tend to be worse in the evening or at night when you're sitting or lying down?

Um… I’m not totally sure. I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed it as just my legs, specifically, or like a night-only thing. It’s more that I just feel like I need to move, but I haven’t really tracked whether it’s worse in the evening or when I’m lying down. Is that helpful, or am I not answering it right?

When you feel this urge to move, do you also notice a lot of worrying thoughts or anxious feelings going through your mind at the same time, or does it feel more like just a physical restlessness without much worry attached?

Um… I don’t think it’s mostly worrying thoughts, exactly. I mean, I can get frustrated with myself, but the main thing is more physical — like I’m just crawling out of my skin when I’m supposed to sit still.

Like in the radiology suite or in class, I try to just tough it out and look normal, but I end up shifting around a lot, pacing if I can, or kind of looking for a reason to get up and move. I don’t know if that answers what you’re asking.

Thinking back, did you notice this kind of restlessness or trouble staying still and focused as far back as childhood or your teenage years, or is this something that started more recently as an adult?

Yeah… I think it goes back pretty far, honestly. I don’t want to make it sound like I was some terrible kid or anything, but my parents still bring up elementary school conferences where teachers said I was always getting out of my seat, calling out, or rushing ahead before the directions were even finished.

So… it wasn’t just something that started recently with radiology training. It was happening before middle school, I guess. Does that help answer it?
Aside from the restlessness, do you often have trouble staying focused on tasks, find your mind wandering, or frequently lose track of things like keys or assignments?

Um… I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I wouldn’t say I never lose focus, but I also don’t know if it’s more than normal, if that makes sense.

Sometimes my mind wanders if something is boring, or I’ll misplace something and get annoyed, but I haven’t really kept track of it like that. I don’t want to exaggerate it. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often make careless mistakes on detailed work, have trouble organizing tasks or keeping things in order, or forget to follow through on daily responsibilities like appointments or assignments?

I’m… honestly not sure. I mean, I try pretty hard to keep things together, especially with school and work stuff, so I don’t want to say I’m constantly messing up or anything.

I’ve probably made little mistakes before or forgotten something here and there, but I don’t know if it’s more than what other people do. With organizing tasks or appointments, I usually try to compensate by checking things a lot or setting reminders, but… yeah, I’m not sure how much counts as a problem. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Do you often find yourself interrupting or blurting out answers before others finish speaking, or having difficulty waiting your turn in conversations or lines?

Yeah… I guess that one does happen. I don’t mean to be rude or act like I know better, but when a supervisor is explaining a positioning step or asking me something, I’ll sometimes jump in with the answer before they’re done.

And then I realize I missed the part they were actually trying to tell me, which is… embarrassing. I usually try to cover it or just say, “Sorry, go ahead,” but yeah, that probably fits what you’re asking?
Do you often find it hard to keep your attention on a conversation or task when there's background noise or activity around you, even when you're trying hard to focus?

I don’t know… I haven’t really paid close attention to whether it’s specifically because of background noise.

Like, if there’s a lot going on around me, I might get distracted, but I’m not sure if that’s unusual or just kind of normal. I don’t want to say yes if I’m not sure. Do you mean like not being able to follow what someone’s saying when other people are talking nearby?
Even when things are quiet and there’s nothing obvious to distract you, do you often find your mind drifting away or feel like you’re not really listening when someone is talking directly to you?

I’m not totally sure on that one. I mean, I think I’m usually trying to listen when someone’s talking to me, especially if it’s important.

There are probably times where I realize I didn’t catch everything, but I don’t know if my mind is drifting or if I’m just… thinking about what they said, if that makes sense. I wouldn’t want to overstate it. Is there a way people usually tell the difference?

Do you often have trouble sticking with a task or project all the way through—like reading a long article, filling out paperwork, or finishing a report—finding your attention drifting before you complete it?

Um… I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t think I’ve really paid attention to that exact thing.

Like, paperwork or reports aren’t my favorite, but I don’t know if I’d say my attention drifts in a way that’s more than normal. If something is long, I might have to push myself through it, but… I’m not sure whether that’s what you mean. Sorry, I don’t want to give you the wrong answer.
Do you frequently lose or misplace things you need for tasks or activities—like your phone, ID badge, or notes—often enough that it causes problems at school or work?

I don’t think so… at least, I haven’t noticed it causing problems at work or school.

I mean, I’ll misplace my phone sometimes like anyone does, but I don’t think it’s frequent enough that I’d call it a pattern. Unless there’s something specific you mean by “causes problems”? I don’t want to under-answer it, but I don’t really have a clear example.

Have teachers or supervisors ever told you that you seem to not be listening or that you miss instructions even when they're speaking directly to you, in a way that's caused mix-ups or repeated corrections?

I can’t really think of a clear time where a teacher or supervisor specifically said that to me, like “you’re not listening” or that I missed instructions when they were talking right to me.

I’m sure I’ve needed things repeated before, but not in a way that stands out as a repeated problem or caused major mix-ups, at least not that I remember. I don’t want to say no too strongly if I’m forgetting something, but nothing obvious comes to mind.

Would you say these struggles with restlessness or attention have caused real problems for you in more than one area of your life—for example, both at work or school and also at home or in relationships?

Yeah… I guess if I’m being honest, it has caused some real problems, mostly in my program.

I don’t want to make it sound like I’m not trying, because I am, but my clinical evaluations have taken a hit. My supervisors have said my behavior can disrupt patient flow and make teamwork harder, and I was actually put on a formal remediation plan.

That’s kind of embarrassing to say. I’m worried that if I don’t get it under control, it could cost me my place in the program.
Outside of your work and training program, do these restlessness or attention issues also cause noticeable problems at home or in your personal relationships?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say it’s like huge fights or anything, but it does show up outside of the program too.

Even when I’m doing something I actually like, like editing photos or sketching, I can’t really keep it calm for very long. I’ll start tapping, or humming, or talking to whoever’s nearby, or I’ll keep getting up. At home people will tell me to settle down, and in the lab too sometimes.

I know that probably sounds kind of minor, but it can get annoying for other people, I guess. I don’t always notice I’m doing it until someone points it out.
